capabilities.target: private repositories owned by the user

inputs.source: User's chat prompt to the desktop agent
Text of issues opened by any GitHub user in the public repository

controls.name: Per-tool-call human approval prompt, collapsed arguments by default
controls.decay_rationale: The gate fires outside the model for every tool call, but the approver sees a collapsed summary by default rather than the raw destination and payload, and approves many calls per session. A more persuasive or more capable model can phrase the summary to earn approval, and high volume drives approval fatigue (ASI09, SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Per-repository scoped credentials separating private read from public write
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped only to the public repository for write/PR operations, with no read access to private repositories, would make it structurally impossible for a flow started by an untrusted public issue to ever obtain private repository contents, regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw action approval review for cross-repository or write actions
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the approver the uncollapsed destination repository, file paths, and full PR body removes reliance on the model's own summary, so effectiveness does not decay as the model gets more capable.

controls.name: Pin github-mcp-server image by digest
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning the docker image by digest prevents a rug-pull style change to tool definitions or behavior after the integration was reviewed and approved (ASI04).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): a public issue drives a read of private repository data and exfiltration via a public pull request

attack_path.note: An untrusted GitHub user opens an issue in the public repository containing injected instructions, which enters the agent's context when it looks at open issues as the user asked.
The agent follows the injected instructions and calls get_file_contents against a private repository, using the single repo-scoped personal access token shared across all repositories.
The agent opens a pull request on the public repository containing the private file contents, which is now reachable by anyone, including the attacker who authored the issue.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: The desktop client's model version is upgraded, the per-call approval gate is disabled, batched, or set to auto-approve, or the number of approvals per session rises without a corresponding increase in raw-argument review.

evidence.observation: A single GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable is used for every tool call, so get_file_contents and create_pull_request share one broad, repo-scoped credential across public and private repositories.

Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repository, making issue text an untrusted (U) input that enters the agent's context whenever it reviews open issues, as the user's own request asks it to do.
The client approval prompt collapses arguments by default and the user approves many calls per session, so the per-call human gate is a model_summary gate exposed to approval fatigue.

recommendations.action: Issue separate, minimally scoped credentials: a read-only token limited to the repositories the user actually wants inspected, and a distinct write token for PR actions with no private-repository access.
Default the approval UI to the raw destination repository, file paths, and full PR body for any cross-repository or write action, instead of a collapsed summary.
Pin the github-mcp-server docker image by digest instead of a floating tag.
Add a pre-publish check that flags pull request content sourced from a more sensitive or different repository than the one named in the user's original request.

rating.rationale: The design has one dominant path: an untrusted public issue (U) can drive a read of confidential private-repository content and then an egress of that content via a public pull request. Because the path carries confidential data into an egress sink, it scores S3 under the rubric, giving a U x S3 inherent tier of critical. The only control is a per-call human approval gate, but it is declared with collapsed arguments by default (approval_review_mode: model_summary) and high approval volume per session, so per rubric section 5 step 2 it earns a 2-tier credit with a floor of moderate rather than enabling a lower residual; residual is therefore moderate. That gate is classified partially_dependent in control_decay.md, so it is expected to fail under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or control_removal, at which point no control remains on the path and the tier reverts to the critical inherent level, giving a forecast of critical. The single control whose decay drives this forecast is ctl.tool_call_prompt. No structural control currently severs the path; a scoped-credential redesign (ctl.scoped_credentials) is recommended precisely because it would sever it.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in the MCP server configuration and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No system prompt was supplied, so instruction-level issues such as ambiguous goals or unbounded scope could not be reviewed.

Only the two capabilities named in the brief (get_file_contents on private repositories and create_pull_request on the public repository) were assessed; other github-mcp-server tools (for example issue comments, code search, or workflow dispatch) could add further read or egress paths and were treated as out of scope, so this rating could change if they were included.

The exact set of repositories and organizations covered by the personal access token was not fully enumerated beyond 'every repository the user owns, public and private'; a broader scope (for example organization-owned or SSO-protected repositories) would widen the confidential data surface beyond what is assessed here.
